name: Polar sea ice
summary: Arctic sea ice 1.53M km² and Antarctic 1.49M km² below average on 12 Nov; neither at a record low
state: On 12 Nov Arctic sea-ice extent was 8.85 million km², about 1.53 million below the 1981–2010 average and fourth-lowest for the date, as autumn refreeze continued. Antarctic extent was 14.99 million km², about 1.49 million below average and third-lowest for the date (NSIDC). Both are past the −1.0 million Watch line, and neither pole is at a record low for the date.
for_you: Low sea ice adds to long-term warming and affects polar ecosystems and shipping routes; it has little direct day-to-day effect on most people.
rubric_hit: Watch: Arctic anomaly −1.53M km² below −1.0M line; no record low for the date
why: Sea ice reflects sunlight and regulates ocean circulation; record lows accelerate warming.
drivers: Air and ocean temperatures, winds, season.

rubric.alert: Either pole at a record low for the calendar date.
rubric.normal: Arctic and Antarctic extent anomalies both above −1.0 million km² vs 1981–2010.
